Reality Fracture is Standard-legal but still carries no arena_id in the card data, so the import list
below becomes playable on Arena once the set is enabled there.

## Overview

The set's prepared mechanic is a free spell stapled to a body: a prepared creature lets you cast a
copy of its back-face spell, and doing so unprepares it. The green-red half of that cycle all shares
the same back face, Soul Tether, which makes a Heartwood token — a red and green artifact that taps
for red or green. Six cards in the deck are Soul Tether creatures, so the deck's first job is to keep
turning bodies into mana rocks.

The second job is what makes it a combo rather than a ramp deck. Draconic Visitor replaces every
artifact token you create with a 5/5 red Dragon with flying. Once it is on the battlefield, Soul
Tether stops making mana and starts making Dragons, Saheeli's Thopters arrive as Dragons, and a
single upkeep with Woodwork Prodigy prepared is a free 5/5 flier every turn.

| Engine piece | Copies | What it does |
|--------------|--------|--------------|
| Heartwood Crafter | 4 | One-mana prepared body; its Soul Tether is a Heartwood, and it taps for colourless mana that cannot pay for spells from hand |
| Konstrari Improviser | 4 | Two-mana prepared body, the cleanest turn-two play, same Soul Tether back face |
| Woodwork Prodigy | 4 | Re-prepares itself every upkeep, so it is the repeatable Soul Tether — one Heartwood or one Dragon per turn, forever |
| Tenured Tethermage | 3 | Two Heartwoods at once, tapped, for the price of a land; also grows itself by tapping two artifacts |
| Aerid Konstrari | 2 | A 5/4 flier that makes a Heartwood on entering and on dying, and pumps itself by the artifact count |
| Draconic Visitor | 3 | The converter: artifact tokens become 5/5 flying Dragons |
| Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar | 2 | Every noncreature spell makes a Thopter, which is a Dragon while Draconic Visitor is out |

## Approach

Plan by phases:

1. Turns 1 and 2: deploy prepared bodies. Heartwood Crafter on one, then Konstrari Improviser or a
   second Crafter. Do not cash the Soul Tether yet unless the mana is spare; the token is worth more
   once there is something to convert.
2. Turns 3 and 4: build the rock count. Woodwork Prodigy and Tenured Tethermage put two to four
   Heartwoods on the battlefield, which is both ramp and the fuel for the combo turn. Karn, Gilded
   Guardian refills the hand off the colours among those artifacts.
3. Turns 5 and up: land Draconic Visitor and convert. From that point every Soul Tether, every
   Saheeli trigger and every Aerid Konstrari death is a 5/5 flier. Craftwork Crusher and Hall of
   Echoes close games that stall on the ground.

Twenty-four lands: fourteen green sources, eight blue and six red, plus every Heartwood token, which
taps for red or green. Karn, Gilded Guardian is counted at two because its hybrid cost is payable
with two generic mana. Twelve cards cost one or two, so the deck is never short of an early play,
and the two seven-drops are the only cards that can sit dead in an opening hand.

## Gameplay strategy

### Early game

Heartwood Crafter is the ideal one-drop: it enters prepared, blocks well enough as a 1/1, and its
mana ability pays for the Soul Tether it is holding. Turn two is Konstrari Improviser, or a second
Crafter plus Artifist Acumen to dig. The important discipline in the first three turns is not to
fire Soul Tether into an empty board. A Heartwood token with nothing to convert is a 2/2-for-three
rate; the same token on the turn Draconic Visitor lands is a 5/5 flier. Fire the tethers when the
mana is otherwise going unused, or when a Tenured Tethermage or Woodwork Prodigy is about to make the
board wide enough that the extra artifact count matters.

### Mid game

Woodwork Prodigy is the engine's centre. It re-prepares during every upkeep, so from turn three it
offers a Soul Tether each turn without spending a card. With Geist of Saint Thalia out, that copy
costs two mana total and can be paid with a Heartwood plus one land. Tenured Tethermage converts a
spare land into two tapped Heartwoods, which is the fastest way to reach five mana for Draconic
Visitor while keeping the board intact. Karn, Gilded Guardian is the mid-game refill: a Heartwood is
two colours, so Karn usually draws two cards on entry and leaves a 5/5 vigilance trampler behind.

### The combo turn

The deck's best turn is the one where Draconic Visitor arrives on a board that already holds prepared
bodies and artifacts. Order it like this: cast Draconic Visitor, then cast every Soul Tether you have
queued. Each copy now creates a 5/5 red Dragon with flying instead of a Heartwood. Woodwork Prodigy
re-prepares at the next upkeep, which is another Dragon. Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar converts each of
those noncreature spells into a Thopter that also arrives as a Dragon, and Puppet Crafting on the
Echoverse Fulcrum gives the board a 5/5 Construct that survives a creature-only sweeper. Two prepared
bodies plus Saheeli is three Dragons in one turn off six or seven mana.

### Win condition two

When the air plan is answered, the deck wins on the ground with artifact bodies. Craftwork Crusher is
a 7/5 trampler that removes a creature or planeswalker and draws a card when it enters, Hungering
Puppetbeast eats spare Heartwoods for +1/+1 counters and a keyword of choice, and Aerid Konstrari
pumps itself by the number of artifacts you control. Hall of Echoes is the land half of this plan:
five mana turns it into a copy of the biggest creature on the board, so the Crusher attacks as two
7/5 tramplers and Draconic Visitor can be doubled for a second conversion effect in the same turn.

### Mulligan guide

Keep two or three lands with at least one green source, one prepared creature, and one payoff —
Draconic Visitor, Karn, Gilded Guardian or Craftwork Crusher. A hand of Heartwood Crafter into
Konstrari Improviser with no five-drop is still a keep, because Woodwork Prodigy and Tenured
Tethermage are common enough that the deck finds its converter by turn five. Ship hands with no
green source, hands whose only lands are Hall of Echoes and Konstrari Annex, and hands with two or
more Draconic Visitor and no early creature.

### Key interactions and edge cases

- Prepared only re-arms through the card's own text or an outside effect. Heartwood Crafter and
  Konstrari Improviser enter prepared once; after their Soul Tether resolves they are vanilla bodies.
  Woodwork Prodigy is the only card here that re-prepares every turn, which is why it is a four-of.
- Draconic Visitor replaces the creation, it does not copy the token. Soul Tether under the Visitor
  makes one 5/5 Dragon and no Heartwood, so the mana rock is gone. Sequence ramp first, conversion
  second.
- Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar triggers on casting, and Soul Tether copies are sorceries, so the Thopter
  arrives before the Soul Tether resolves. With the Visitor out that Thopter is a 5/5 Dragon.
- Tenured Tethermage's land sacrifice is optional and it is a real cost: only take it with four or
  more lands, or when the two Heartwoods immediately pay for a five-drop.
- Karn, Gilded Guardian counts colours among other artifacts you control. A Heartwood is both red and
  green, so one Heartwood is already two cards; the deck has no other multicoloured artifact, so
  expect two, not five.
- The Echoverse Fulcrum's five-mana ability destroys all creatures, Dragons included. It is a reset
  button for the turn the opponent has committed more than you, not a removal spell.
- Puppet Crafting can enchant any non-Aura artifact, so a Heartwood token is a legal target and stays
  a mana rock while it is a 5/5. Enchanting the Echoverse Fulcrum makes the sweeper body-safe.
- Hall of Echoes taps for colourless only. Two copies are utility, not mana fixing; do not count them
  as green or red sources when keeping a hand.
- Craftwork Crusher's choose-two modes are picked on entry, and the damage mode can hit a planeswalker
  or clear a blocker before the trample damage is assigned.

### Matchups

Against aggro the deck is soft: there is no removal spell in the list, so the plan is to trade
Heartwood Crafter and Konstrari Improviser early, land Karn as a 5/5 blocker, and race with Dragons
from turn five. Against midrange it is a favourite, because the token engine goes wider than most
midrange boards and Craftwork Crusher answers their best creature on entry. Against control, hold
Draconic Visitor until you can cast it with a Soul Tether or a Saheeli trigger behind it, and lean on
Karn and the Echoverse Fulcrum to keep cards flowing; a single Visitor that resolves usually ends the
game in two attacks. Against combo, the deck has no interaction beyond damage, so it must mulligan
toward the fastest curve and count on flying Dragons closing before the opponent's engine comes
online.
